function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! The best place to order a cake depends a bit on where you’re located and what kind of cake you’re after. Here’s a quick rundown of the most common options:

| Option | What it offers | How to order | Tips |
|--------|----------------|--------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for special occasions | Call or visit the shop, or use their website if they have one | Ask about flavor combos, dietary restrictions, and delivery times. |
| **Online cake delivery services** | Nationwide or regional delivery, many design templates | Browse the site, pick a design, customize, and checkout | Check delivery windows, read reviews, and confirm the cake arrives on time. |
| **Grocery stores & supermarkets** | Ready‑made cakes, sometimes custom orders | Pick up in‑store or order online for pickup/delivery | Great for quick orders; check the “specialty” or “bakery” section. |
| **Food‑delivery apps (Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, etc.)** | Cakes from local restaurants or bakeries | Search “cakes” or “desserts” in the app | Delivery fees apply; check the restaurant’s rating. |
| **Specialty dessert shops (e.g., Magnolia Bakery, Levain Bakery)** | Signature cakes, often with a unique twist | Order online or call ahead | These shops can be pricey but are worth it for a special treat. |
| **DIY kits (e.g., King Arthur Baking, Bakeology)** | All‑in‑one cake‑making kits | Buy online or at a craft store | Fun if you want to bake yourself but still want a “cake” delivered. |

### Quick starter list (U.S. based)

| City | Bakery / Service | Contact |
|------|------------------|---------|
| New York | **Magnolia Bakery** | 212‑555‑1234 / www.magnoliabakery.com |
| Los Angeles | **Baked by Melissa** | 310‑555‑5678 / www.bakedbymelissa.com |
| Chicago | **The Cake Shop** | 312‑555‑9012 / www.thecakeshop.com |
| Seattle | **Seattle Cake Company** | 206‑555‑3456 / www.seattlecakecompany.com |
| Online (nationwide) | **BakeShare** | www.bakeshare.com |
| Online (nationwide) | **Amazon Fresh** | www.amazon.com/fresh |

> **Pro tip:** If you’re ordering for a special event (wedding, birthday, corporate), it’s a good idea to place your order at least 2–3 weeks in advance. That gives the baker time to prep and you time to tweak any last‑minute details.

---

#### Need help narrowing it down?

If you let me know your city or zip code, I can pull up a few highly‑rated local options and even check their current availability. Just drop me a line!
